ground_truth: The change adds the module-level `EmailAttachment = namedtuple("Attachment", ["filename", "content", "mimetype"])` in `django/core/mail/message.py`. `EmailMessage.attach()` now stores each attachment as an instance of it. Pickle serializes namedtuple instances by looking up the class by its `__qualname__` ("Attachment") in its module. No `Attachment` attribute exists in `django.core.mail.message`; the class is bound to the name `EmailAttachment`. As a result, pickling an `EmailMessage` with any attachment fails with a `PicklingError` (attribute lookup Attachment on django.core.mail.message failed), e.g. `msg.attach("a.txt", "x", "text/plain"); pickle.dumps(msg)`, which breaks queuing emails through task queues or caches. The fix renames the namedtuple type names to match their variable names (`namedtuple("EmailAttachment", ...)`, and likewise `EmailAlternative`).
